summary: Upgrading from the iPhone 14 Pro Max to the iPhone 18 Pro Max offers substantial generational improvements across nearly every category after a four-year gap. The new flagship features a larger 6.9-inch display, an advanced triple-lens camera system with a variable physical aperture, a faster 2nm A20 Pro processor, and 60W USB-C charging. Additionally, it provides exclusive access to Apple Intelligence and advanced Siri AI features that the older model cannot support.
key_points: The iPhone 18 Pro Max starts at $1,199 with 256GB of baseline storage, compared to the iPhone 14 Pro Max starting at $1,099 with 128GB.
The display is upgraded to a 6.9-inch panel with a 3,000-nit peak brightness and an anti-reflective coating.
The camera system features a 48MP main sensor with a variable physical aperture, a 48MP telephoto sensor with 4x optical zoom, and Pro Controls.
Charging speed is significantly faster, upgrading from the 14 Pro Max's 20W Lightning connection to 60W wired charging via USB-C.
The iPhone 18 Pro Max supports Apple Intelligence and the revamped Siri AI, whereas the iPhone 14 Pro Max lacks the hardware for these features.

title: Apple's iOS 27 is already here while we wait for Samsung's One UI 9
author: Mihai Matei
content:
Published: September 15th, 2026 at 21:00 UTC+02:00
One of these days, Samsung will hopefully take notes.
Abhijeet Mishra / SamMobile
September 14 may not be significant to Samsung fans, but it was an exhilarating day for iPhone users everywhere. Apple started rolling out the iOS 27 update on that date, and for us, it only serves as a reminder of what Samsung is doing wrong, or at least what it could do better.
We're referring to OS update schedules and rollouts. We've discussed this before, but Samsung still can't match the precision with which Apple controls new iOS releases.
What's different between Apple's and Samsung's firmware methods? In short, Apple is able to set the right expectations and then deliver.
In more concrete terms:
Meanwhile, Samsung still hasn't announced a concrete release date for One UI 9, more than a month after the first Galaxy devices (the Galaxy Z8 foldables) that come preloaded with One UI 9 went on sale.
One UI 9 is still in beta testing for older devices, including the S26 series, with no concrete release date in sight. The closest we've gotten to an announcement was a Samsung Community forum post a couple of weeks ago, claiming that the stable version of One UI 9.0 for the Galaxy S26 series will roll out “soon.”
Well, it hasn't been soon enough. And, you guessed it: Once Samsung does start rolling out stable One UI 9, it won't go as smoothly as iOS 27. Rollout dates will vary not only by device but also region.
September 14 has reminded us once again that if there's anything Apple does better than Samsung, it's how it handles firmware updates. Samsung's method has improved in recent years but still can't hold a candle to Apple's well-oiled update machine.
The good news, at the very least, is that One UI 9 on the latest Samsung foldables works like a charm. Hopefully, the same experience will translate to other Galaxy devices once they receive the stable update, whenever that may be.
summary: Apple released its iOS 27 update on September 14, highlighting the ongoing contrast between Apple's precise update rollouts and Samsung's slower firmware schedule. Samsung still has not announced a concrete release date for One UI 9 for older devices, leaving the stable version in beta testing. Additionally, when Samsung eventually rolls out One UI 9, the release will likely vary by device and region, unlike Apple's more controlled deployment.
key_points: Apple began rolling out iOS 27 on September 14, 2026.
Samsung has not yet announced a concrete release date for the stable version of One UI 9.
One UI 9 remains in beta testing for older devices, including the Galaxy S26 series, more than a month after new foldables launched with the software preloaded.
Samsung's rollout dates for One UI 9 will vary by both device and region.

title: Is bankrupt Level Up Giveaways boss Anton Hall behind new scheme?
author: Steve Jones
content:
![A man with short black and grey hair and facial hair depicted in a graphic used in one of his competitions. Behind him are gold coins, Â£50 notes and text which reads 'Win Â£1000 every week'.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1920/cpsprodpb/e0bf/live/53afbda0-acf4-11f1-bc1f-3f186ca4140c.png)
Ex-Level Up Giveaways director Anton Hall, pictured in this composite image, has been running new pay-to-enter competitions
- Published
When Ami Shuttleworth and her fiance Chris Smith were told they had won Â£10,000 in a pay-to-enter competition, they immediately knew how they would spend their prize.
"We were over the moon, our wedding was going to be paid off," recalls the 34-year-old mother-of-one from Middlesbrough.
Mel Higgins, 33, also had big plans for the Â£5,000 she was told she had won.
"I was going to pay off my credit card and whatever was left I was going to put into my business," says the driving consultant from Chippenham.
"I cried my eyes out because I thought, 'this is going to change my life'."
Yet, like many others who were successful playing with Level Up Giveaways, neither of them received a penny of their winnings.
The firm, based in Sowerby Bridge in West Yorkshire, was wound up at the High Court in August 2025 over unpaid debts, with its sole director, Anton Hall, also made bankrupt in November 2025 as part of separate proceedings.
The BBC understands the company owed tens of thousands in unpaid prizes to its customers before it stopped trading.
Admin assistant Ami says she "saw red" when she found out 37-year-old Hall is now involved in a new prize draws venture.
"Like a lot of people I'm just angry," she adds.
For Mel, "it just feels wrong".
Running a business, either directly or indirectly, would breach the terms of Hall's bankruptcy order and constitute a criminal offence.
Hall, who according to court documents is now living in York, told the BBC: "I haven't set up or owned a limited company, and I'm not a director of, or managing, a limited company.
"The competitions I hosted have been run personally through the Raffall platform."
Raffall is an independent website which allows people to host their own competitions.
Sometimes referred to as prize draws or pay-to-enter competitions, these enterprises work by selling a set number of entries to a draw, often for a cash prize.
The Department for Culture, Media and Sport has described prize draws and competitions as a "significant and growing market".
![Mel Higgins, a young woman with strawberry blonde hair and black-rimmed glasses. She is smiling in the photo, a selfie, a wearing red lipstick.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1536/cpsprodpb/8288/live/7f57d130-a160-11f1-aaf8-119f176ff4ce.jpg)
Mel Higgins did not receive the Â£5,000 she won with Level Up Giveaways
Government legislation on bankruptcy restrictions states: "You need the permission of the court to act as a company director.
"This includes directly or indirectly, taking part in, or having a concern in the promotion, formation or management of a limited company."
There are no restrictions on a person who is bankrupt working as an employee of a company.
In a YouTube video released in August, Hall said he would be an employee of the new venture, which would be run by someone else.
However, he appears to have played a leading role in promoting and running the enterprise, which is also in his name.
In a series of social media posts since announcing the new venture, he suggested he was personally managing draws and openly discussed sales numbers, profit and loss figures and guiding the future direction of the venture.
Raffall founder and CEO Stelios Kounou confirmed the account @antonlevelup was registered to Hall personally and said payments had been made only to an account held in the name of Anton Hall.
The account had been set up prior to Hall being declared bankrupt, Kounnou added.
Kounou said Raffall had been contacted by the Insolvency Service, which manages Hall's bankruptcy, regarding the account.
A spokesperson for the Insolvency Service said they did not comment on individual cases.
![An Instagram post from an account linked to Anton Hall which makes reference to him running competitions as part of the new venture, which is in his name.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1376/cpsprodpb/c6d9/live/fc038e20-ad01-11f1-beae-535b95a24b3e.png)
Hall's social media posts hint at him running the competitions
Discussing his new venture last month, Hall said the feedback had been "good", adding: "A few people negative, understandably, I get it - potentially the winners from Level Up Giveaways who didn't get paid unfortunately.
"We have agreed that if [the new venture] takes off - it's a big if - and it starts making a decent amount of profit we are going to look at trying to pay out people who didn't get paid from Level Up Giveaways.
"That is the ultimate goal."
Hall's bankruptcy restrictions, which last 12 months, will expire on 7 November.
They include having to tell the trustee of his bankruptcy about any additional income on top of what has already been declared.
This money could be used to pay back creditors over a period of three years.
Hall said he had "not made any net profit" from running the draws.
The BBC asked him how he was able to make promises about the payment of potential future profits of the new enterprise, given he was an employee.
He said the video was recorded "before I became aware of the bankruptcy proceedings and related restrictions".
"At that time, I was discussing working with someone else on a proposed business, but once I became aware of the situation, that proposed arrangement did not proceed."
After he was contacted by the BBC, Hall suggested he would no longer be running competitions in a social media post.
"The raffle thing isn't worth putting my family through the drama," he wrote.
![An Instagram post from the @winwithanton account which shares profit and loss figures from prize draws he has ran. The overall figure shows a loss of more than Â£1,000](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1376/cpsprodpb/618e/live/52e088e0-adc7-11f1-a540-61c3f7fc4e6c.png)
Hall's latest venture has also lost money, according to his social media posts
Ami and Chris had previously won Â£10,000 with Level Up Giveaways in 2023 during seemingly better times for the company.
But the following year, when they thought they had once again been successful, the firm's problems appeared to mount, with numerous winners left in the dark.
In a YouTube video published in January 2025, Hall said he has been struggling to sell enough tickets for his draws to cover costs, leaving him unable to pay out.
Yet the comeptitions continued.
Ami recalls making "phone call after phone call" chasing her winnings.
"It did cause a lot of stress in the lead up to the wedding," she remembers.
"It didn't take the shine off our wedding, but it's always going to be in the back of my mind how it could have changed it."
Mel says her experience has been "hugely upsetting".
"Fair enough things go wrong and people do make mistakes, but when you are that far into it you have got to pull the plug and stop taking money from people."
Pointing to a recent social media post from Hall promoting a competition which he claimed had undersold, she adds: "I'm pretty sure that behaviour got him into the mess in the first place."
summary: Anton Hall, the former director of the bankrupt pay-to-enter competition firm Level Up Giveaways, has faced scrutiny over his involvement in a new prize draw venture. Level Up Giveaways was wound up in August 2025 owing tens of thousands in unpaid prizes, with Hall declared bankrupt in November 2025. While Hall claimed he was merely an employee hosting competitions through the Raffall platform, social media posts and platform records suggested he played a leading role in running the new enterprise. After being contacted by the BBC, Hall indicated in a social media post that he would no longer be running competitions.
key_points: Level Up Giveaways was wound up in August 2025 due to unpaid debts, leaving numerous customers without their promised cash prizes.
Sole director Anton Hall was made bankrupt in November 2025.
Running a business directly or indirectly while bankrupt breaches bankruptcy terms and is a criminal offence.
Platform records and social media posts suggested Hall was personally managing and promoting a new prize draw venture.
Following inquiries by the BBC, Hall stated on social media that he would no longer be running competitions.

title: Hundreds of contractors are reportedly reading real ChatGPT conversations
author: Ana Maria Constantin
content:
![Photo of a laptop showing ChatGPT app Photo of a laptop showing ChatGPT app](https://media.thenextweb.com/2026/07/openai-kalshi-chatgpt-world-cup-prediction-markets.avif) 
ChatGPT app
OpenAI is paying hundreds of contractors to read real ChatGPT conversations and rate the chatbot’s replies under the internal codename Project Lily, and did not answer when asked where it had told users. The Court of Justice held last September that a controller’s duty to inform applies at collection and does not depend on whether the recipient can identify anyone.
OpenAI is paying hundreds of contractors to read real ChatGPT conversations and rate the chatbot’s replies, under the internal codename Project Lily, 404 Media reported.
The reviewers do not see usernames. They can see a user memories summary above the prompt, which sometimes shows what the person has used the chatbot for before and where in the world they may live.
OpenAI says a Privacy Filter model strips personal information first. Its own page for that model says it can make mistakes, miss uncommon identifiers and under-redact when context is limited.
404 Media asked the company to point to where it tells users that humans may read their chats. OpenAI did not answer, and after publication pointed to a help page.
Anthropic confirmed it uses human review too, for users who switch the setting on, and says it removes account identifiers first. Google’s Gemini carries a line saying humans review some saved chats.
Europe settled the part that matters here last September.
The Court of Justice held in EDPS v SRB that a controller’s duty to inform people applies before any transfer, and is judged from the controller’s own point of view rather than the recipient’s.
So whether a contractor in North America could work out who wrote a prompt is not the test. The obligation sat with OpenAI at the moment it collected the conversation.
Italy’s regulator has already fined the company EUR 15M, nine of it for processing without an adequate legal basis, and ordered six months of public information advertising on Italian television and radio.
The default matters as well. Improve the model for everyone is switched on for free, Plus and Pro accounts, and off for Enterprise, Business and Edu, and switching it off applies to new conversations rather than old ones.
OpenAI has spent the year selling privacy to the other half of its market, previewing zero data retention for enterprise customers in August.
Consumers get the setting that feeds the model.
“I don’t think they would imagine some contractor somewhere is analyzing the conversations,” one reviewer said. The same company has been asking those users to connect their bank accounts.

summary: OpenAI is employing hundreds of contractors to read and rate real ChatGPT conversations under the internal codename Project Lily. While OpenAI utilizes a Privacy Filter to strip personal information, the filter's documentation notes it can make mistakes and under-redact data. The company did not answer when asked where it informs users that humans may review their chats, though legal obligations regarding data collection and transparency remain a significant issue.
key_points: OpenAI pays hundreds of contractors to review and rate real ChatGPT conversations under the codename Project Lily.
Reviewers can see user memory summaries that occasionally reveal past usage and geographical locations.
OpenAI's Privacy Filter model, meant to strip personal information, is acknowledged to sometimes miss uncommon identifiers and under-redact data.
OpenAI did not directly answer questions regarding where it informs users that human contractors read their chats.
Italy's regulator previously fined OpenAI EUR 15M for processing data without an adequate legal basis.

title: Reminder: iOS 27's All-New Siri AI Has a Waitlist, Here's How to Sign Up
author: Joe Rossignol
content:
Apple this week released iOS 27 following around three months of beta testing. If you just installed the software update on your iPhone, you might be wondering where the new-and-improved Siri AI and dedicated Siri app are. In case you missed it, you must join Apple's waitlist in order to gain access to these new features.
![Personalized Siri iOS 27](https://images.macrumors.com/t/uDGySbpuSNItG5nCDRDrMOEJgDs=/400x0/article-new/2026/06/Personalized-Siri-iOS-27.jpg?lossy)
Keep in mind that while iOS 27 is compatible with the iPhone 11 and newer, Siri AI is limited to the iPhone 15 Pro and newer. This is because Siri AI requires an iPhone model that is compatible with Apple Intelligence, which we have listed below.
Fortunately, joining the Siri AI waitlist is a simple task:
- Open the Settings app on your iPhone.
- Tap on the Siri menu.
- Tap on Try Siri AI (Beta).
- Follow the prompts.
Wait times seem to vary, with some users receiving access to Siri AI within a few minutes of signing up and others having to wait a few hours or even days.
You will receive a notification on your iPhone once you have received access to Siri AI, and the Siri app will automatically appear on your device at that time. You can talk or type to Siri AI in three ways: swipe down on your iPhone's Dynamic Island, press and hold your iPhone's side button to invoke the assistant, or open the Siri app.
The classic version of Siri has always been useful for basic actions like setting a timer and checking the weather, but it has notoriously struggled with more advanced requests over the years. Siri AI is much more intelligent and personalized: it is essentially a ChatGPT-like version of Siri that can respond to most questions.
Siri AI can draw on your personal information stored on your iPhone, has on-screen awareness, and can perform actions in more apps that support it.
The new Siri is limited to English to start, but Apple said support for French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish will be available in October, likely as part of the release of iOS 27.1. Apple said Siri AI has unspecified daily usage limits, but it noted that expanded access will be coming with select iCloud+ plans.
Siri AI is not available in the EU on iOS 27, iPadOS 27, and watchOS 27 at launch, as Apple is in a regulatory battle with the European Commission.
The following iPhone models are compatible with Siri AI:
- iPhone 18 Pro
- iPhone 18 Pro Max
- iPhone Duo
- iPhone 17e
- iPhone 17
- iPhone 17 Pro
- iPhone 17 Pro Max
- iPhone Air
- iPhone 16e
- iPhone 16
- iPhone 16 Plus
- iPhone 16 Pro
- iPhone 16 Pro Max
- iPhone 15 Pro
- iPhone 15 Pro Max
You can adjust Siri AI's pace and expressivity on these iPhone models:
- iPhone 18 Pro
- iPhone 18 Pro Max
- iPhone Duo
- iPhone 17 Pro
- iPhone 17 Pro Max
- iPhone Air
Apple still considers Siri AI to be in beta even though iOS 27 is no longer in beta overall.
summary: Apple has released iOS 27, which includes a new-and-improved Siri AI feature that requires users to join a waitlist through their device settings. The advanced, ChatGPT-like assistant is restricted to specific newer iPhone models and is not available in the EU at launch. Users receive a notification and automatic app installation once granted access, though wait times vary from minutes to days.
key_points: Users must sign up for a waitlist in the iOS 27 Settings app to access the new Siri AI.
Siri AI requires compatible iPhone models starting from the iPhone 15 Pro and newer.
Wait times for access range from a few minutes to several hours or days.
The new assistant is initially limited to English and is not available in the EU on iOS 27.
Siri AI features on-screen awareness, personalization, and integration with supported apps.

title: Apple CarPlay quietly just got a free upgrade with some long-awaited additions
author: Roger Fingas
content:
The amount of attention Apple throws at CarPlay can vary wildly. Sometimes, it barely mentions the tech during major press events, if at all. At other times, it's centerstage -- say when executives are trying to pitch CarPlay Ultra to both automakers and iPhone owners alike.
The iOS 27 update might be classified somewhere in between. That makes sense, since while there's one giant change Apple wants you to focus on, the others are harder to sell as dramatic improvements. They could have a meaningful impact on your commute, however, since they include a few things iPhone owners have long demanded.
Siri AI
Voice commands, now actually useful
I did make ample use of Siri in CarPlay prior to iOS 27, but mostly because it was the only way I could send and receive texts while driving. It wasn't too useful otherwise, as it was hard to gauge whether a particular command would be understood. Even when an action was supported, you often had to use a narrow vocabulary, which isn't necessarily convenient when you're trying to focus on traffic.
Siri AI should solve that, since it's based on the same generative AImodels found in Google Gemini. It allows for more natural conversations, including direct answers to more knowledge questions, instead of prompting you to check your iPhone when you stop. Apple has also implemented "app intents" -- really, shorthand for a deeper level of app integration. Hypothetically, you could ask CarPlay to "play that song Jackson really likes in Spotify" and it would identify the song from your Messages chat. You might also ask how much time is left on a parking meter, or whether the hotel you're heading to has a continental breakfast -- that data could be extracted from a variety of sources, all without violating privacy.
You may need to be patient, though. Developers with CarPlay apps need to build out their intents, and there could be a crush on Apple's servers for a while. Also, your iPhone needs to support Apple Intelligence, which means an A17 Pro chip or later.
Media scrubbing and mini-players
Frickin' finally
Somehow, it took until iOS 27 for Apple to understand that CarPlay users expect to drag or tap on the progress bar to skip forward and back. That's how it works when you're using a native iPhone app, after all. The change might not matter a lot for music, but podcast listeners can finally skip past unwanted ad blocks without asking Siri, or else repeatedly tapping or holding other buttons. For audiobook and podcast fans alike, it should be a shortcut when you inevitably lose your progress.
Some audio apps -- primarily Apple Music -- now also include built-in mini-players. These present basic play/pause and skipping controls when you're in other parts of an app, saving you the trouble of having to go back to a "now playing" view while you're browsing for something. This might actually matter most to parents, say if you're listening to a soul playlist and not quite sure your kid should be hearing Twin Temple just yet.
Video playback
No, you can't watch Golden Girls while you drive
Much as on Teslas and some other vehicles, you can now watch videos when you're parked, even taking advantage of AirPlay. Well, sort of. There are additional limits at the moment. You first need a compatible dash system, meaning one with H.265/HEVC decoding, 4GB of memory, and 1080p resolution. That nixes most older cars, and good luck finding the specs for any dash. On top of that, "select apps" is doing a lot of heavy lifting. There's no official roster, so you might need to wait a while for your favorite app to join the chorus.
What's the point of video when you're parked? The auto industry is slowly transitioning to EVs, and here in North America, that can mean spending 20 minutes or more at a charging station when you can't charge at home. But really, even people stuck with gas-powered vehicles often want to kill time in a better manner than Wordle or Reddit, and a 10-inch screen with surround sound is preferable to phone playback.
New wallpapers
Why no custom ones, Apple?
When you pop open the in-car Settings app, you'll notice that Apple has added a bunch of new wallpapers to match what's on your iPhone. These are all based on the same pattern, but sport alternate colors that might better suit your personality and/or the vehicle you're driving. Also, different versions pop up if you switch CarPlay's appearance between Light and Dark.
What's baffling to me is that Apple still hasn't enabled support for custom wallpapers, as on iPhones. This may be a matter of quality control. As much as you might love your spouse or dog, that badly-shot living room photo could be in the wrong aspect ratio, clash with app icons, or simply be too small to match your car's display. With stock wallpapers, there's no question about whether they'll meet resolution and contrast standards.
summary: The iOS 27 update for Apple CarPlay introduces several long-awaited features and improvements designed to enhance the driving and parked experience. Key upgrades include generative AI-powered Siri for more natural conversations, media scrubbing and mini-players for audio apps, parked video playback support, and new stock wallpapers. However, these features come with hardware requirements, such as requiring an iPhone that supports Apple Intelligence or a compatible dash system for video.
key_points: Siri AI integration provides more natural voice conversations and deeper app integration using app intents.
Media scrubbing allows users to finally drag or tap progress bars to skip forward and back in audio apps.
Built-in mini-players for apps like Apple Music offer basic playback controls while browsing other sections.
Video playback is now supported when the vehicle is parked, though it requires specific dash hardware and compatible apps.
New stock wallpapers matching iPhone designs are added to CarPlay settings, though custom wallpapers are still not supported.

title: iOS 27 launch day: 8+ features to try right away
author: Matt Binder
content:
![iOS 27 logo](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/01K6Q0EmfluFTXmoRF1AjkM/hero-image.fill.size_1248x702.v1789408500.jpg) 
iOS 27 is here! The newest iPhone operating system has just been rolled out by Apple today.
Here are a few of the must-try features that you should check out as soon as your iPhone is finished updating to the new OS.
Siri AI
This is the big one. Apple has completely reimagined its voice assistant Siri as a full-fledged AI assistant.
You May Also Like
Siri AI can now perform tasks and answer questions just like other AI assistants like ChatGPT and Claude. But, of course, Siri AI is integrated directly into the iOS experience. Siri AI even has its very own app now.
The new Siri AI can take actions across a wide variety of apps, such as a user's email, phone, photos, and Shortcuts. Siri AI can even create a new Shortcut based on a simple description. Users simply vocalize the workflow they want to automate in plain English, and Siri AI will take over and set the whole thing up.
So, be sure to check out Siri AI both via the standalone app (and the custom voice controls) to see what the brand new Siri can do.
![siri ai custom voice options](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/01K6Q0EmfluFTXmoRF1AjkM/images-1.fill.size_536x750.v1789410407.png) 
Weather app updates
The Weather app has some big new updates in iOS 27 to take a look at.
There are new tabs for the day's weather that provide users with information about conditions, precipitation, and Wind. Each tab will provide more in-depth details about the current day's temperature, rain or snow, and the wind conditions over the next few hours.
There's also a new Highlights feature in the Weather app that provides users with a written summary of what to expect weather-wise throughout the day.
AirPods custom EQ
![custom eq settings in ios 27 with airpods](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/01K6Q0EmfluFTXmoRF1AjkM/images-2.fill.size_2000x1124.v1789410407.jpg) 
Surprisingly, AirPods have been missing custom EQ settings, a standard feature for most headphones and earbuds. Well, no longer.
iOS 27 adds a three-band equalizer to the AirPods settings screen, allowing users to control the audio frequency spectrum of their earbuds.
Users can adjust EQ in real-time, changing how they hear the bassy lows, vocal mids, treble detail in the highs, and more.
Other headphones have this capability and Apple previously allowed AirPods users to customize EQ within Apple Music. Now, however, AIrPods owners can have this greater audio control regardless of where they listen to their music.
Liquid Glass updates
![new liquid glass slider in ios 27](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/01K6Q0EmfluFTXmoRF1AjkM/images-3.fill.size_2000x2000.v1789410407.png) 
If you had some problems with the way Apple's new Liquid Glass design for iPhone looked, you may want to go directly to this new feature.
Apple has updated the Liquid Glass design with "more uniform refraction and improved contrast." The iPhone-maker has even added controls in the form of a new slider that allows users to change just how clear or tinted the Liquid Glass design appears.
Disable the dictation button in Messages
This is another fix to an issue that has long-annoyed some iPhone users.
There's a dictation button next to the text box in Messages. That dictation button becomes the "Send" button when you've already typed out some text in your message. However, the placement of both buttons makes for some accidental taps, which sometimes activate the dictation feature when it isn't wanted.
Now, in iOS 27, users can change that in the iPhone settings. Simply open the Settings app, select Apps, then Messages, followed by the new Show Text in Field option. Users can pick if there's a Record Audio button, Start Dictation button, or no button at all in that spot. The Send button will obviously still appear as normal after a user starts typing.
Bill splitting
If you're tired of trying to figure out the math of who pays what when going out for a meal with friends, this new iOS 27 feature is a must-try.
Using Apple Wallet or the Messages app, simply point your iPhone camera at a receipt, iOS 27's new bill splitting feature will read the information and then provide an itemized list on your iPhone. From there, you can pick which items you're paying for and then use Apple Cash to just pay for what they ordered. The bill-splitting feature even adds the relevant tax and tip portion as users select what items they are paying for.
Photo app updates
By now, you've probably heard about the big iOS 27 updates to the Photos app. Clean Up, Extend, and Spatial Reframing utilize generative AI in order to completely transform your photos, remove unwanted objects, and change angles and perspectives.
But there are other lesser talked about new features to check out too.
For example, iPhone users can now share albums with their friends who own Android and Windows phones with the new iOS 27. In addition, users can now select stills from videos and save them as standalone pictures instead of having to take screenshots.
iPhone Handoff
This is probably the most undercovered feature, especially if you're someone who can't choose between your classic iPhone or the new foldable iPhone Duo.
iPhone Handoff lets you have both.
With iOS 27's new iPhone Handoff feature, Apple smartphone owners can use one number with two separate devices. Users can swap back and forth and pick which device will receive phone calls and messages, and then switch it back at any time.
For now, this feature is only available for T-Mobile users, and the carrier is charging an extra $5 per month to use it.
There's even more to check out with the new iOS 27, so be sure to explore the latest updates to your iPhone.
Preorder the new Apple products
Along with iOS 27, Apple also released new AirPods, Apple Watches, and iPhones. Except for the iPhone Duo, all of these devices are available for preorder now.
![Apple AirPods 5 earbuds](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/product/01v2E915osFJIM67WEyUCyt/hero-image.fill.size_256x242.v1789080996.jpg) 
![apple watch series 12](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/01K6Q0EmfluFTXmoRF1AjkM/images-4.fill.size_222x256.v1789410407.jpg) 
![Apple iPhone 18 Pro, 256GB](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/product/02UTmeBAT7zGEng4qZQXBsp/hero-image.fill.size_256x256.v1789142199.png) 
![iPhone 18 Pro Max, 256GB](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/product/06oJDWmYcQr0OpQSPw0t8cL/hero-image.fill.size_256x256.v1789142619.png) 
![Matt Binder](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/authors/03D9P4Ol8cUK8wCTnrmWxbl/image.fill.size_100x100.v1723243678.png) 
Matt Binder joined Mashable's tech vertical in 2018, where he covers social media, tech policy, cybersecurity, online scams, cryptocurrency, AI, creator news, weird tech, and other related tech beats.
![Mashable Potato](https://mashable.com/images/seamless-keep-scrolling.png)
summary: Apple has officially rolled out iOS 27, introducing a wide range of new features and updates for iPhone users. Key additions include a reimagined Siri AI assistant, custom EQ settings for AirPods, and new options for the Weather, Photos, and Messages apps. Users can also take advantage of bill splitting via Apple Wallet, Liquid Glass design controls, and the new iPhone Handoff feature.
key_points: Siri has been redesigned as a full-fledged AI assistant with its own app and the ability to take actions across various apps.
AirPods now feature a three-band equalizer for real-time audio frequency adjustments.
The new bill-splitting feature uses the camera to read receipts in Apple Wallet or Messages, allowing users to pay for their items using Apple Cash.
iPhone Handoff allows users to share one phone number across two separate devices, currently available for T-Mobile users.
Messages now includes an option to change or disable the dictation button next to the text box to prevent accidental taps.

title: Porting Half-Life: Alyx to Steam Frame: How Valve's Engineers Went from "There's No Way" to Shipping Standalone
author: Digital Foundry; William Judd
content:
![Porting Half-Life: Alyx to Steam Frame: How Valve's Engineers Got It Running Standalone 1](https://images.digitalfoundry.net/9dda13b1137f4/porting-half-life-alyx-to-steam-frame-how-valves-engineers-got-it-running-standalone-1.970x.jpg)
When the Steam Frame was announced, the idea that a high-end VR showcase like Half-Life: Alyx would run natively on a modestly powerful, ARM-based headset seemed far-fetched - and Valve set expectations accordingly. Even earlier, the mood internally was simple: "this is never going to work." Yet, as Valve engineers used Alyx as a test-bed for standalone games on the headset, progress came surprisingly swiftly, and Alyx is shipping alongside Frame as a fully native game on the system.
Speaking to project lead and gameplay programmer Robin Walker and engineer Autumn Ashton, who did much of the port work alongside years on SteamVR, Steam Deck and driver development, that initial scepticism was well founded: Alyx was never designed to be squeezed. As Walker puts it, Alyx was the result of "overinvesting resources" to build "our best attempt at what a VR game could be." He goes to say that the team "didn't make any real compromises around performance or anything, because that was antithetical to the goal."
What shifted the calculus was hardware. Streaming to Frame was always going to be a good experience, but as the platform's feature set came together, a native build started to look less absurd. "As you start to get more features and the stack working - foveated rendering, eye tracking, and the fact that the headset has 16 gigs of RAM - it made us think 'maybe, maybe we could get there with some work'," says Ashton. Walker positions gaze-driven rendering as the thing that made the whole project thinkable: "I think the foveated rendering and eye tracking was this potential silver bullet. We didn't know how much value we were going to get out of that, but that was sort of the shining star or guiding light."
Ashton began hacking on a prototype, and immediately ran into the most fundamental difference between the two targets: Frame's GPU is a tiler, whereas a desktop part is an immediate-mode renderer. That distinction is invisible to players and brutal to a renderer that wasn't written with it in mind. "Half-Life: Alyx occasionally would break rendering to go do something else for a bit, then come back to it, and that has a much bigger cost on the Steam Frame than it would on a desktop," Ashton explains. The work was less a single architectural rewrite than an audit: "finding all these death by 1,000 cuts type things to go and find fixes for them - that was the main thing."
The prototype was enough to prove the idea, and Walker is candid that what followed was not glamorous. After that first milestone roughly 18 months ago, he says, "it's not particularly sexy, I guess, but then there's just a year and a half of grinding software work as we work through drivers, new features in SteamVR and so on." That grind is arguably the real story of the port, because very little of it lives inside Alyx itself. The overwhelming majority of the performance came from beneath the game.
Ashton makes the point that Alyx's value to Valve was as much diagnostic as commercial. "Half-Life: Alyx was a really good forcing function for getting other parts of the stack into shape for us to ship the Steam Frame," she says. "We discovered so many things in driver, so many things that we needed from the SteamVR side - that even if we didn't ship Half-Life: Alyx on Steam Frame, doing that one and a half years of work... it was completely worth it." Walker adds the strategic framing: driver and compositor work on new hardware is normally speculative, an attempt to guess at the shape of software that doesn't exist yet, and "it was super useful to have, for once, an extremely clear target: we need to make that thing run as well as it possibly can." Alyx, he notes, is "a superset of a lot of the problems that people have run into on VR".
The iteration speed that made 18 months of driver work possible came from the open-source stack. "We wouldn't have been able to do any of this without having open-source drivers, because we were iterating so quick," says Ashton. "You could have a problem, we'd see it in Alyx or any other game in the catalogue that we're helping third-party developers bring up, and we can have something testable within minutes potentially, instead of weeks or months away if you're working with a third-party vendor on drivers." It's a practical argument for Valve's Mesa-based approach, and it applies well beyond this one title.
![Porting Half-Life: Alyx to Steam Frame: How Valve's Engineers Got It Running Standalone 3](https://images.digitalfoundry.net/9bdb926c4d6cd/porting-half-life-alyx-to-steam-frame-how-valves-engineers-got-it-running-standalone-3.970x.jpg)
When it comes to performance, Alyx renders at 36fps on Frame and is re-projected upward, but the technique is more sophisticated than a simple timewarp. "We're running at 36fps, but we're using depth reprojection," Ashton says. Using a hand held in front of the face as an example, she describes the parallax problem: the hand and the background move at different rates as you shift, and a naive reprojection can't reconcile them. "If we provide a depth texture from Alyx, or any other game provides a depth texture, we can incorporate that information into reprojection, so that even if you're doing this, we can be completely smooth. You wouldn't be able to tell." Alyx doesn't supply motion vectors, and the implicit motion-smoothing path in SteamVR that handles that case remains in beta - but many third-party VR developers already had motion-vector pipelines feeding the compositor, so Valve brought that route up first and those titles benefit too.
Image quality rests on eye tracking, and Ashton is unequivocal about its necessity: "I don't think it would have been shippable without having eye tracking giving us the gaze information to feed into foveated rendering." SteamVR exposes a fragment density map that developers can either consume automatically via the injection layer or author themselves for tighter control, and dialling in Alyx's own map was hand-tuning rather than automation - "probably about a week of going through a lot of content and all the different resolution levels that we wanted to tune it for". Only a couple of Alyx's shaders needed adjusting for the architecture; as Ashton notes, "the overarching majority of the work was done in the driver and SteamVR.
Perhaps the most consequential decision was one of restraint: Valve refused to touch the game's content. The team asked itself what version customers would most want shipped, and, as Walker explains, "it seemed really clear that the most valuable version would be one where we didn't go and change a bunch of content." The reason is the Workshop. "There's a vast amount of content in the Half-Life: Alyx Workshop these days, and if we went and changed a bunch of content to make Alyx run, that content would be unlikely to work, or we'd be asking Workshop people to come back and [make changes] - that's just not going to happen." The gap between a Frame version where all that community content simply works and one where it doesn't was, he says, "really, really significant". Valve's regard for that community is not abstract either. "We have hired multiple people now because of the work they did in Half-Life: Alyx levels."
The knock-on benefits are the ones players will feel. Because nothing was forked, Steam Cloud saves and crossplay work across Windows, Linux and Steam Frame, so you can take the streamed, higher-resolution PC experience at your desk and pick up the same save standalone. Controller support needed a pass but not a rewrite, since Alyx already carried a translation layer for the several headsets and controllers in circulation at launch; Ashton recalls changing "the backpack height very slightly on Steam Frame just to make it easier," and little else. The per-controller work, Walker notes, is stubbornly manual - just a case of going in and tuning it "until it feels as good as you can". Stutter, meanwhile, is handled by the Steam Shader Cache, which records a game's shaders and either delivers them precompiled or builds them server-side, so "as soon as you start playing a game, you're playing with a fully filled shader cache".
Where does this leave everyone else? Ashton is careful not to overclaim on Alyx's behalf: the route for third parties runs less through this port than through compatibility tooling such as FEX and Lepton, the goal being that developers can ship one build rather than several. Valve had its own in-house option here - the core engine was already running on ARM thanks to its past work on Dota and Artifact - which most studios won't, hence the emphasis on offering a menu of paths rather than a mandated one. Both are clear that the investment continues after launch, in the Steam Deck mould, where titles that ran at launch simply ran better a year on.
The most interesting takeaway, though, is the one Walker offers about Valve's own assumptions about the capabilities of native VR headsets: "Man, we really should be expecting more on our native work... we had decided there was just limits on what we could do in our native stuff that were probably accurate at some point, but they've just become inaccurate, and we weren't challenging ourselves enough." His hope is that the lesson spreads - that gamers and developers alike realise that "we can push native games further".
It will be fascinating to see how the arrival of Steam Frame affects the PC and standalone VR spaces, especially if we do see an uptick in the fidelity of standalone experiences. It's clear that Valve has worked hard on the whole ecosystem, not just the headset itself, and there's plenty more planned to improve performance and add features to this new ecosystem. It's hard to see Steam Frame becoming as mainstream as the Steam Deck when it costs over $1000, but a full pipeline means that Frame's value should at least improve over time.
summary: Valve engineers successfully ported Half-Life: Alyx to run natively on the standalone, ARM-based Steam Frame headset. Despite initial skepticism due to the game's high resource demands, hardware features like 16GB of RAM, eye tracking, and foveated rendering made the project viable. The 18-month development process focused heavily on optimizing drivers, SteamVR, and open-source Mesa-based tools rather than altering the game's core content or Workshop compatibility.
key_points: Valve successfully brought Half-Life: Alyx to the standalone Steam Frame headset as a fully native title.
Hardware capabilities like eye tracking and gaze-driven foveated rendering were crucial to making the port possible.
The vast majority of performance improvements came from a year and a half of grinding software work on drivers and SteamVR rather than changing the game's content.
Open-source drivers allowed for rapid iteration, enabling engineers to test fixes within minutes.
Valve deliberately avoided modifying the game's content to ensure full compatibility with existing Half-Life: Alyx Workshop community creations.

title: Google rolls out Motion Assist bubbles to Pixel, Samsung
author: Abner Li
content:
![](https://9to5google.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/4/2026/09/Android-Motion-Assist-cover.jpg?quality=82&strip=all&w=1600) 
After announcing earlier this month, Google has rolled out Motion Assist to Pixel and Samsung phones running Android 17.
The aim is to reduce motion sickness when you’re in a car, bus, or other moving vehicle with an onscreen bubbles overlay that adjusts to the device’s motion.
To enable, search for “motion assist” in the Settings app or open the Quick Settings editor and scroll down to “From system apps” (on Pixel). The long route is Settings app > Google > All services tab > Personal & device safety > Motion assist. Part of Google Play services, it appears alongside Advanced Protection and Theft protection.
![](https://i0.wp.com/9to5google.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/4/2026/09/Android-17-Motion-Assist-2.jpg?ssl=1)
![](https://i0.wp.com/9to5google.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/4/2026/09/Android-17-Motion-Assist-1.jpg?ssl=1)
This menu lets you have Motion Assist automatically “Start in a moving vehicle,” but Google also recommends adding a Quick Settings Tile to manually enable and disable “from any screen.” Once active, there’s also a silent system notification that lets you disable with a tap. On most phones, you get two columns of shapes on the left and right edges.
The Customize menu lets you adjust:
- Color: Based on system (Dynamic Color), Red, Yellow, Green, Blue
- Shape: Circle, Square, Pentagon, Diamond
- Opacity: Slider
- Randomization: “Color and shape change every few seconds”
As of today, Motion Assist has widely rolled out on all our Google Pixel and Samsung Galaxy (Fold 8 series) devices running Android 17. Be sure to restart your phone if it’s not yet live. We’re seeing the bubbles with version 26.33.32 of Google Play services.
![](https://i0.wp.com/9to5google.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/4/2026/09/Android-17-Motion-Assist-3.jpg?ssl=1)
![](https://i0.wp.com/9to5google.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/4/2026/09/Android-17-Motion-Assist-4.jpg?ssl=1)
![Add 9to5Google as a preferred source on Google](https://9to5google.com/wp-content/themes/ninetofive/dist/images/google-preferred-source-badge-dark.png) 
![Add 9to5Google as a preferred source on Google](https://9to5google.com/wp-content/themes/ninetofive/dist/images/google-preferred-source-badge-light.png)
summary: Google has rolled out the Motion Assist feature to Pixel and Samsung devices running Android 17. The tool uses an onscreen bubbles overlay that adjusts to vehicle motion to help reduce motion sickness. Users can enable the feature through device settings or a Quick Settings tile, and customize its color, shape, opacity, and randomization.
key_points: Motion Assist is available on Pixel and Samsung phones running Android 17.
The feature aims to reduce motion sickness using onscreen bubbles that react to vehicle movement.
It can be found in the Settings app under Google Play services or toggled via a Quick Settings tile.
Users can customize the appearance of the bubbles, including color, shape, opacity, and randomization settings.

title: Xbox's Asha Sharma Wants To Better Understand Players, So She's Helping With Customer Support
author: Pure Xbox; Fraser Gilbert
content:
![Asha Sharma Wants To 'Better Understand Players', So She's Helping With Xbox Customer Support](https://images.purexbox.com/4a99221b9d90b/asha-sharma-wants-to-better-understand-players-so-shes-helping-with-xbox-customer-support.900x.jpg)
Back on Friday, the folks over at The Wall Street Journal shared a report about new Xbox boss Asha Sharma, describing her as "The Woman Fixing a Microsoft Mess With Brutal Honesty", and getting insights into the kind of person she is.
Most of it is stuff we've already heard before — that she's a hard-worker, that she's intense, that she's been extremely successful in past positions at the likes of Porch and Facebook — and there are even comments in here from people like Bethesda's Todd Howard who describe her as "uniquely effective at cutting through and communicating clearly".
What's probably most interesting for us is the bit at the end, which mentions that Sharma actually spends a few hours per-month replying to Xbox customer support tickets in order to "better understand players".
Here's the direct quote about that:
"To better understand players, she spends a few hours each month responding to customer support tickets, during which she’s learned how complex it can be to fix a single player’s problem."
As you'd perhaps expect, there are already people out there questioning the legitimacy of this quote and whether the whole thing is just a "PR piece", but we doubt they'd throw in such a specific thing like this if there wasn't truth to it.
In fact, Sharma herself apparently has a mantra of "clarity is kindness" at Xbox, and we've certainly seen that during her time in charge - she's been clear about her mission briefings when it comes to big changes such as the "Xbox Reset", and we've also started to see Xbox being praised for their transparency around Xbox Live outages.
There have been big highs and lows during Asha Sharma's reign as head of Xbox so far, but the general consensus on her seems to be positive amongst Xbox fans as things stand, and clearly she's put in a ton of work to get up to speed on the gaming industry in a short space of time. There's a long road ahead - the era of Asha is just getting started!
summary: Xbox boss Asha Sharma spends a few hours each month answering customer support tickets to better understand players and the complexities of solving their issues. A recent report highlights her intense work ethic, clear communication style, and efforts to bring transparency to Xbox. While some question the PR angle of the support ticket story, her overall leadership has largely garnered a positive consensus among fans.
key_points: Asha Sharma spends a few hours each month responding to Xbox customer support tickets.
The practice helps her understand players and the complexity of fixing their problems.
Colleagues describe her as uniquely effective, hardworking, and direct in her communication.
Her leadership has brought increased transparency to Xbox, including clearer communication regarding outages.

title: How to prepare your iPhone for the iOS 27 update - Engadget
author: Jack Peachey
content:
How to prepare your iPhone for the iOS 27 update
A quick checklist of pre-update preparations will help your iOS 27 upgrade go smoothly.
iOS 27 introduces a variety of design and UI refinements, as well as a sizable revamp to Siri AI to compete with the big names in the space. Thankfully, iOS 27 works on phones as old as the iPhone 11. If your device is compatible with this update, it's wise to get prepared before you install it.
You'll need to make sure your phone has the space and power to usher in the upgrade, plus you have to decide how you want to run it: automatically overnight, or as soon as it becomes available.
How to ensure a smooth transition to iOS 27
First, there are the core requirements. The update process requires room for temporary files along with the main download, so you'll want to have a good amount of free space. Try to have around 18 to 25GB available, using unconventional ways to clean up your iPhone if you're currently low.
You'll also need enough power to update your device. While 50 percent battery life should be enough to get you through the process, it's much safer to keep your phone plugged in while updating. Keep your phone connected to Wi-Fi too.
Furthermore, you'll need to decide if you want to start the update yourself or let it run automatically. Head to Settings > General > Software Update > Automatic Updates to configure this. If you choose Automatically Install, your phone won't start installing iOS 27 as soon as it's available. Rather, it will update when charging and connected to Wi-Fi overnight. You might get a notification about this, which could be days or weeks after the update becomes available. To start the update manually instead, wait on the Software Update page.
While you're considering this, you should also check if you've updated to iOS 26.6, which includes an indexing update to make the shift to iOS 27's Siri changes smoother.
Back up your phone before iOS 27's big changes
Importantly, don't forget to back up your device. Installing any update, especially major ones like iOS 27, can lead to issues and possible data loss. You can back up through iCloud by visiting Settings > Apple Account > iCloud > iCloud Backup > Back Up Now. Alternatively, back up your data to a Mac or Windows PC. You should also make sure you have your Apple ID credentials handy to keep yourself from being locked out if something happens.
Carrying out these measures will make the upgrade process far smoother and prepare your device for the wealth of goodies arriving with iOS 27. Chief among these features is the new Siri app in iOS 27, Apple's attempt to catch up to competitors like Gemini and ChatGPT. This version also brings a more readable design, faster performance, new child safety features and many tweaks to other iOS apps.
summary: Preparing your iPhone for the iOS 27 update involves ensuring sufficient storage space, battery power, and a stable Wi-Fi connection. Users should also back up their devices to iCloud or a computer and decide whether to install the update manually or automatically overnight. Additionally, users are advised to update to iOS 26.6 first for a smoother transition to the new Siri features.
key_points: Ensure you have 18 to 25GB of free space available for temporary files and the main download.
Keep your phone plugged into power and connected to Wi-Fi during the update process.
Back up your device to iCloud or a Mac or Windows PC before installing the major update.
Configure your update preference to install either manually or automatically overnight.
Update to iOS 26.6 beforehand to help make the shift to iOS 27's Siri changes smoother.

title: Apple unveils its first foldable - the iPhone Duo, iPhone 18 Pro official, Week 37 in review
author: Ivan
content:
Of course, Apple dominated the most popular stories of week 37 this year. Apple held a historic event on September 9 - the first in new CEO Ternus' reign, and the one to finally unveil the first foldable iPhone.
Interestingly, the iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max scored more hits than the iPhone Duo. Apple's latest Pro models got a variable aperture main lens, a faster A20 Pro SoC, and a smaller Dynamic Island. The iPhone 18 Pro series is now on sale, starting from $1,200/€1,450 and $1,300/€1,600, respectively, and will begin shipping on September 18.
The iPhone Duo is, undoubtedly, the star of the show. Apple's first foldable looks every bit the cutting-edge piece of tech everyone expected. It's a wide-styled foldable, about the size of a passport when folded. Its inner display is anti-reflective, has a less-visible crease, and is seemingly seamless, thanks to an under-display camera. Oh, and Touch ID is back! The iPhone Duo is shipping in October and costs $2,000/€2,300.
The eSIM-only 18 Pro Max gets the longest battery life in iPhone history.
Apple has entered the foldable smartphone chat, and it's bringing the goods.
The 18 Pro series is $100/€150/£100 more expensive than the 17 Pro generation.
The new iPhones are set to launch on September 9.
Thanks to the EU's Energy Labels, we got the actual capacities of the iPhone 18 Pro series batteries. The 18 Pro has a 4,056mAh cell, while the Pro Max has a 5,391mAh one.
Back to the Duo. The natural comparison that people will make is to Samsung's Galaxy Z Fold8. We ran the numbers, but you can bet we'll do a full in-depth look at the pair once we get them in the same room.
Only for the models with the physical SIM card slot, however, but it's more than nothing.
A detailed spec rundown between the two foldables.
The three models each have their own strengths and weaknesses - here are the ones that we think matter the most.
And in the only two non-Apple stories that were able to sneak by, we got the design reveal of the Honor Magic9 series and the vivo X500 series.
The Honor Magic9 series will debut in China on September 28. As for the vivo X500 Pro Max, it packs a massive circular rear camera island, in keeping with its predecessors. It will also support the teleconverter zoom lens.
The vivo X500 series will be unveiled on September 21.
The series is also available for pre-order in China.
summary: Apple dominated tech news during week 37 by unveiling its first foldable phone, the iPhone Duo, alongside the iPhone 18 Pro series. The iPhone Duo features a passport-like wide design, an under-display camera, and Touch ID, with shipments starting in October at $2,000. Meanwhile, the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max are already on sale starting at $1,200 and $1,300 respectively, featuring upgrades like a variable aperture lens and an A20 Pro SoC.
key_points: Apple unveiled its first foldable phone, the iPhone Duo, priced at $2,000/€2,300 with an October shipping date.
The iPhone 18 Pro series is already on sale starting at $1,200 for the Pro and $1,300 for the Pro Max.
The iPhone 18 Pro models feature a variable aperture main lens, a faster A20 Pro chip, and a smaller Dynamic Island.
The eSIM-only iPhone 18 Pro Max features the longest battery life in iPhone history, housing a 5,391mAh battery.
Non-Apple news included the upcoming launches of the Honor Magic9 series and vivo X500 series in September.

title: World Of Warcraft Might Be Coming To Console As New Xbox 'Controller Support' Revealed
author: Pure Xbox; Fraser Gilbert
content:
![World Of Warcraft Might Be Coming To Console As New Xbox 'Controller Support' Revealed](https://images.purexbox.com/9ef8db07608e3/world-of-warcraft-might-be-coming-to-console-as-new-xbox-controller-support-revealed.900x.jpg)
Ever since Xbox acquired Blizzard a few years ago, we've constantly questioned why they haven't decided to bring World of Warcraft to consoles, but it looks like that might actually be about to change in the not too distant future.
Following yesterday's announcements at Blizzcon 2026, people in attendance were able to go and check out the new World of Warcraft: Forever game for themselves, and they were greeted by a new "gamepad option" that was described as being in an "alpha state" - with the team looking for feedback on it.
Here's a glimpse at the poster that people saw, along with various in-game views as well:
Speaking to ScreenRant as part of the event, a couple of team members explained that World of Warcraft: Forever will definitely have Xbox controller support (on PC) at launch this year, but that there are "a lot of design questions to ask" when it comes to adding controller support to the "Retail" version of World of Warcraft in particular.
However, they did highlight that Retail kind of already has controller support using add-ons:
"So Retail does sort of have controller support using add-ons. Official out-of-the-box support is something we're super excited to add in Forever. Never say never for features like that [for Retail]. I think there are a lot of design questions to ask when you look at Modern World of Warcraft compared to Classic or Forever, just with the amount of key binds. But again, I think that the benefits you get from accessibility are obvious here. So we're going to pay a lot of close attention to how people react to the out-of-the-box controller support for Forever."
In other words, should World of Warcraft find its way to console in the not too distant future, it's probably going be in the form of WoW: Forever and/or Classic, while the Retail version might take a little longer to surface.
No announcements have been made at all about a console version for World of Warcraft just yet, but considering they're putting so much effort into adding Xbox controller support, surely it's just a matter of time. Fingers crossed!
We'll leave you with a closer look at yesterday's announcement of World of Warcraft: Forever down below.
summary: Recent announcements at Blizzcon suggest that World of Warcraft could eventually come to consoles following the introduction of official Xbox controller support. Attendees discovered a new gamepad option in an alpha state for World of Warcraft: Forever. While developers confirmed that Forever will feature out-of-the-box Xbox controller support on PC at launch, bringing it to the Retail version presents more design challenges due to the large number of key binds.
key_points: World of Warcraft: Forever will feature out-of-the-box Xbox controller support on PC at launch this year.
A gamepad option in an alpha state was showcased for attendees at Blizzcon.
Developers noted that Retail World of Warcraft has more design challenges and key binds to consider before getting official controller support.
No official announcements have been made regarding a console release for the game yet.

title: Deals: iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max pre-order begins, Galaxy Z Fold8 and Galaxy S26 series get discounted
author: Siddharth
content:
Apple’s brand new iPhone 18 Pro series is now available for pre-order, with sales set to begin on September 18. Meanwhile, pre-orders for the iPhone Duo will start in October, but if you can’t wait that long, Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold8 and Z Fold8 Ultra are both on sale this week.
The iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max look similar to last year’s iPhone 17 Pro series, but are available in new colorways. The new iPhones also get the new 2nm A20 Pro chipset and feature a variable aperture main rear camera.
Apple has increased the prices of both the new Pro models, so if you’d like to save some money, the iPhone 17 Pro and 17 Pro Max are available with discounts up to £150.
If you’re interested in the new iPhone Duo, Apple’s first foldable, then you’ll have to wait until October 16 to pre-order it, with sales set to start on October 23.
The iPhone Duo features a 7.6-inch inner flexible display and a 5.4-inch cover screen. Both displays offer a 4:3 aspect ratio. It’s powered by the A20 Pro chipset as well, but makes do with a dual-rear camera setup.
One of its main competitors is Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold8, which is currently available with a discount of up to £250. The Z Fold8 has a similar passport-like design as the iPhone Duo.
If you’re looking for an even larger screen, the Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra is also up to £250 off its launch price, making it a great deal.
Want something smaller? The Galaxy Z Flip8 is available with a price cut as well.
The latest Samsung Galaxy Z foldables are all powered by the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 for Galaxy chipset.
Notably, Samsung’s entire Galaxy S26 lineup is also currently on sale, including the newly launched Galaxy S26 FE. The Galaxy S26 Ultra is £400 off right now, whereas the Galaxy S26+ gets a £370 price cut. Meanwhile, the Galaxy S26 is available with a discount of £250.
The Galaxy S26 FE is also on sale, but you’re only going to save £50 off its launch price.
It comes with a 6.7-inch AMOLED display, the Exynos 2500 chipset, a 4,900mAh battery, and a triple-rear camera setup.
We may get a commission from qualifying sales.

Older models like the iPhone 17 Pro series and various Samsung devices, including the Galaxy Z Fold8 series and the Galaxy S26 lineup, are currently receiving notable discounts.
key_points: Apple's iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max are available for pre-order ahead of September 18 sales, featuring the A20 Pro chipset and higher prices.
Apple's first foldable phone, the iPhone Duo, will be available for pre-order on October 16 with sales starting October 23.
Previous-generation iPhone 17 Pro models are discounted by up to £150.
Samsung's Galaxy Z Fold8, Z Fold8 Ultra, and Z Flip8 are currently on sale with price cuts of up to £250.
The entire Samsung Galaxy S26 lineup, including the Galaxy S26 Ultra and Galaxy S26 FE, is currently discounted.

title: GTA 6 shares 7 new gameplay details as its November launch draws nearer
author: Olly Smith
content:
![GTA 6 shares 7 new gameplay details as its November launch draws nearer](https://resizer.ladbiblegroup.com/unsafe/rs:fit:3840:0:0:0/g:sm/q:70/aHR0cHM6Ly9ldS1pbWFnZXMuY29udGVudHN0YWNrLmNvbS92My9hc3NldHMvYmx0YmMxODc2MTUyZmNkOWYwNy9ibHQxZGZmZmMwYTAwYTUzN2VhLzZhYTI3MzQ0NmJhMzcyOTRhYTM2NDM1NC9ndGFfNi5qcGc.webp)
Grand Theft Auto VI fans have been treated to seven new gameplay details ahead of the November release, and it’s mostly stuff that wasn’t seen in last month’s Extended Look.
We went for many years without so much as a lick of information about Grand Theft Auto VI outside of what was seen in the trailers, but now it seems like we’re getting an abundance of info courtesy of Rockstar Games and those who have seen the game in action.
One of the most detailed interviews for GTA VI has now been published online, where Famitsu spoke with Rockstar co-studio head Rob Nelson who revealed more about the game.
Here are some of the highlights we can pick out from the interview (translated via GTAVice.net).
Alternative ways to use guns
![GTA 6,](https://resizer.ladbiblegroup.com/unsafe/rs:fit:3840:0:0:0/g:sm/q:70/aHR0cHM6Ly9ldS1pbWFnZXMuY29udGVudHN0YWNrLmNvbS92My9hc3NldHMvYmx0YmMxODc2MTUyZmNkOWYwNy9ibHRiOTMzZWJkOWMyYTAxNDZmLzZhOWZmOWQ2MWIyMTFkYjdiYzA0ZWZmNy9ndGEtNi1wb2xpY2UtY2hhc2UtbHVjaWEuanBn.webp)
Advert
Nelson revealed that players opting for a more pacifist playstyle can opt to deliberately miss their shots and fire near an NPC to frighten or confuse them, which may buy yourself time to escape.
We imagine this’ll come in handy for any missions where there are NPCs that you don’t want to harm. Jason and Lucia seem a little bit more level headed than previous GTA protagonists like Trevor or Niko, so it seems like a decent option if you don’t want to kill civilians.
Nelson also revealed that suppressive fire is a thing you can do as well, cutting off enemies from flanking you, returning fire, or reaching an objective.
Home comforts
Nelson revealed that there are many small details inside Jason and Lucia’s home. In the preview, Jason was seen pulling back the covers next to a sleeping Lucia and sluggishly climbing into bed. The next day, you’ll see the characters having their morning coffee.
Nelson says, “This is an extremely small detail, but inside the house you can't just throw things like mugs down wherever you want. It's a space where the two of them live, so you have to carry a mug somewhere it can properly be placed. You can't put it directly on the floor; you have to take it somewhere appropriate and put it down.”
Map details
Nelson revealed that the in-game map will reveal information about certain activities you can do in Vice City, such as finding gang hideouts, showing entry points you can use to sneak inside and steal cash or drugs.
“The map can even tell you how much cash and how many drugs are being stored at a hideout, and you can take stolen drugs to a fence. You can also rob jewellery stores or small banks either alone or as a pair,” Nelson says.
Dress to impress
According to Nelson, there are “thousands of outfits”, a lot more than what was available in Grand Theft Auto V, and you’ll also obtain new clothing items by either purchasing them from stores or completing missions.
“As we also announced when pre-orders were revealed, this game has more customisation options than ever before, including a wide variety of hairstyles,” Nelson adds. “There are countless clothing stores and hair salons scattered around the map. You can cut your hair at a hideout as well, but the customisation options there are limited. If you want to try lots of hairstyles, you’ll have to go to a salon.”
More details about robberies
Nelson also spoke a bit about how robberies work, revealing that you can do these heists either alone or in pairs. He also says that you can go in loud through the front entrance or adopt a sneakier route, and the shop security will affect your approach.
“We approach through the back entrance so we won't be spotted, but kicking the door down would trigger the alarm. We have a snap gun — a special lock-picking tool — so let's sneak inside instead. Once inside, if you destroy the security cameras, nobody can see you. If you disable the security system, the alarm won't go off either. In this way, you can quietly steal cash from the store register. If you simply leave afterward, nobody will know what happened there.”
Stealing cars
![GTA 6,](https://resizer.ladbiblegroup.com/unsafe/rs:fit:3840:0:0:0/g:sm/q:70/aHR0cHM6Ly9ldS1pbWFnZXMuY29udGVudHN0YWNrLmNvbS92My9hc3NldHMvYmx0YmMxODc2MTUyZmNkOWYwNy9ibHRlYzZmMjY5YzFkZDI1MWVkLzZhOGQ1NzAyM2Q2ZmU3NjQ4YTRjNjEzNy9KYXNvbl9hbmRfTHVjaWFfcmV0cm9fVmljZV9jaXR5X2Nhcl9pbl9HVEFfNi5qcGc.webp)
Stealing a vehicle and evading police is a lot more complicated in Grand Theft Auto VI compared to previous entries. Depending on the value of the vehicle, stealing a car may require more effort. Cheaper cars you simply need to break into, but more valuable cars later on require you to obtain a digital key cloner and may be fitted with alarms.
“If the car you’re trying to steal is a luxury vehicle, you’ll need the key cloner. There’s also a high probability that it will have an alarm and a sophisticated tracker. Even if you manage to steal it, while you’re driving slowly for a while, the tracker may transmit a signal and allow the police to determine your location,” Nelson says.
Police aggression
Nelson also mentioned police aggression, revealing that police will start searching for your stolen vehicle if the car owner reports it as stolen. They don’t know your exact location, but will begin an investigation based on available information such as your clothing, appearance, and the car you’re driving. This state is called “Heat”, where you remain a suspicious person even after shaking off the cops.
“If you throw away the weapon you were carrying during the robbery, you can lower the level of suspicion at the cost of losing it. If your clothing and appearance are also known, you can escape the Heat by taking clothes off. If you change clothes in a clothing store and disguise yourself, you no longer match the information from the report and can safely escape,” Nelson explains.
“The police search the Heat Area, which is the area covered by the Heat, and as long as you remain inside it, the Heat won’t disappear. But if you can get outside the Heat Area, the pursuing police disappear. Leaving the area entirely is therefore one method of escape. However, you still can’t relax simply because the police have left the scene. If you get into a vehicle that has already been identified, there’s still a risk of being spotted by police.”

title: The iPhone Duo didn't reinvent Android foldables, but I fear the copycats anyway
author: Ben Schoon
content:
![](https://9to5google.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/4/2026/09/iphone-duo-3.jpg?quality=82&strip=all&w=1600) 
Apple’s first foldable is here and, shocker, it didn’t exactly reinvent the foldable, but the iPhone Duo did get some of the most important aspects right, and will give the Android side of the conversation some things to work on too.
This issue of 9to5Google Weekender is a part of our newsletter that highlights the biggest Google stories with added commentary and more. Sign up here to get Weekender delivered to your inbox every weekend, and catch our weekday roundups too!
Look, I promise we’ll stop talking about the iPhone Duo at some point. We’re not 9to5Mac, but Apple’s first foldable is a big deal for the Android side of the industry too. It’s not every day that an entirely new form factor built up by Android brands gets co-opted by the only real competitor.
And, despite Android’s several-year head start, Apple is immediately putting up a fierce competition with its iPhone Duo.
It’s a polished foldable across the board. A smart design with aspect ratios that should prove useful – and, based on the Fold 8’s popularity, resonate among customers – and a package that seems to deliver on everything it needs to. It’s thicker and heavier than basically every other current Android foldable, but it’s also not so far out of the ordinary as to be uncompetitive. Early reactions have been positive, though I’m certainly curious to see what people think after the typical Apple event psychosis wears off.
But, as good as the Duo looks, I think the biggest thing to walk away with is that Apple is not reinventing the foldable. It’s been speculated for years now that Apple would somehow crack open the formula on how to build a foldable in ways that no Android brand had figured out and, based on what’s been shown off so far, that’s simply not the case.
On the hardware side, Apple doesn’t seem to outdo existing hardware in any particularly meaningful ways. The matte display is the thing that has my attention most, as it seems to lessen even the visual appearance of a crease to essentially nothing – though, without that, I bet it’d be similar to the Galaxy Z Fold 8 and Oppo Find N6. But even that display doesn’t seem flawless, with the glossy dot over the selfie camera immediately catching my attention. Under-display cameras are already a tech that’s been shown to be of dubious worth, and with this visual oddity at play, I’m pretty surprised Apple adopted this one at all.
![](https://9to5google.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/4/2026/09/iPhone-Duo-hands-on-2.jpg?quality=82&strip=all&w=800)
![](https://9to5google.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/4/2026/09/iPhone-Duo-hands-on-1.jpg?quality=82&strip=all&w=800)
The software is where even I expected Apple to figure out ideas for a foldable beyond what we’ve seen but, really, there wasn’t much.
Split-screen looks mostly akin to the Pixel Fold, though with the two halves treated as independent by default and allowing you to go to the homescreen to grab another app. That feels very intuitive, even if Android has the same core functionality through its taskbar. The ability to put video windows on top of other apps looks useful and more polished than existing split-screen or picture-in-picture options on Android, but it’s still not exactly groundbreaking.
![](https://9to5google.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/4/2026/09/iphone-duo-1_59c436.jpg?quality=82&strip=all&w=800)
![](https://9to5google.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/4/2026/09/iphone-duo-2.jpg?quality=82&strip=all&w=800)
The most attention-grabbing additions in Apple’s software come from a neat animation that shows up when you open or close the device – almost certainly set to be copied in future software updates on Android devices – and a rethinking of navigation.
Apple is moving app controls and the status bar to the side of the UI rather than the top and bottom where they’re resided for ages now. It gives me mixed feelings. The utility of offloading those controls to the side of the display to make vertical content feel more at home on the wider aspect ratio makes sense, but it also looks wildly ugly to me, or unbalanced at the very least.
All of this is to say, Apple didn’t break any new ground here, and they still have to deal with many of the same problems.
Like every existing foldable, Apple has some different ideas to add into the core experience, but that core experience is essentially the same – it’s just based on iOS this time. Android “got it right” in terms of that core experience, and now everyone has a chance to sit down and think about where to take it next. In a way, it reminds me of the whole app drawer situation. Android got this right years ago, and Apple brought in its own version that’s the same core idea, just different (and much worse, but I digress).
What worries me is the idea that Android manufacturers are going to rush to copy what Apple has put out.
There’s nothing on the iPhone Duo, at least not yet, that feels worth copying – except maybe that aforementioned animation. The sidebar setup, for instance, acknowledges a problem that these new form factors are facing. Modern smartphones are all tall and narrow slabs, so wide designs aren’t a thought for developers. By offloading everything to the side, Apple is presenting a solution for the lack of space for content that devices like Fold 8 have to give up for the sake of top and bottom bars. I’m just personally not sure it’s the right solution. As just one example, this UI decision sounds awful for anyone who uses their phone in their left hand (which, hello, that’s me). At least the top and bottom bars are equally a little bit uncomfortable for everyone.
![](https://9to5google.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/4/2026/09/iphone-duo-sidebar-1.jpg?quality=82&strip=all)
It’s a bold new chapter in the foldable market, and Apple is surely set to sell a lot of these. I’m perhaps most surprised that it’s competitively priced – cheaper than Samsung’s top foldable, too! On top of that, I think the Duo will be a net-positive for Android foldables in the long run. The creativity of iOS developers could bring some new ideas to Android in time as new eyes look at these form factors, and it’s also going to force accessory makers to finally take foldables seriously.
What do you think of the iPhone Duo and how it relates to Android foldables?
